arxiv-1908-11279.title: Grounded Agreement Games: Emphasizing Conversational Grounding in Visual Dialogue Settings
arxiv-1908-11279.creator: David Schlangen
arxiv-1908-11279.description: Abstract Where early work on dialogue in Computational Linguistics put much emphasis on dialogue structure and its relation to the mental states of the dialogue participants (e.g., Allen 1979, Grosz & Sidner 1986), current work mostly reduces dialogue to the task of producing at any one time a next utterance; e.g. in neural chatbot or Visual Dialogue settings.

arxiv-2106-03288.title: Quivers and moduli of their thin sincere representations in Macaulay2
arxiv-2106-03288.creator: Mary Barker, Patricio Gallardo
arxiv-2106-03288.description: Abstract . We introduce the Macaulay2 package ThinSincereQuivers for studying acyclic quivers, the moduli of their thin-sincere representations, and the reflexive flow polytopes associated to them. We provide some background in the topic and illustrate how the package recovers examples from the literature. 1.

arxiv-2310-19965.title: On the number of neighborly simplices in R d \mdmathbb{R}^{d}
arxiv-2310-19965.creator: Andrzej P. Kisielewicz
arxiv-2310-19965.description: Abstract Two d d -dimensional simplices in R d \mdmathbb{R}^{d} are neighborly if its intersection is a ( d − 1 ) (d-1) -dimensional set. A family of d d -dimensional simplices in R d \mdmathbb{R}^{d} is called neighborly if every two simplices of the family are neighborly.

arxiv-2406-19008.title: VertiMRF : Differentially Private Vertical Federated Data Synthesis
arxiv-2406-19008.creator: Fangyuan Zhao, Zitao Li, Xuebin Ren, Bolin Ding, Shusen Yang, Yaliang Li
arxiv-2406-19008.description: Abstract . Data synthesis is a promising solution to share data for various downstream analytic tasks without exposing raw data. However, without a theoretical privacy guarantee, a synthetic dataset would still leak some sensitive information. Differential privacy is thus widely adopted to safeguard data synthesis by strictly limiting the released information.

arxiv-2412-03736.title: Domain-specific Question Answering with Hybrid Search
arxiv-2412-03736.creator: Dewang Sultania, Zhaoyu Lu, Twisha Naik, Franck Dernoncourt
arxiv-2412-03736.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Dewang Sultania, Zhaoyu Lu, Twisha Naik, Franck Dernoncourt. Domain-specific question answering is an evolving field that requires specialized solutions to address unique challenges. In this paper, we show that a hybrid approach—combining a fine-tuned dense retriever with keyword-based sparse search methods—significantly enhances performance. Our system leverages a linear combination of relevance signals, including cosine similarity from dense retrieval, BM25 scores, and URL host matching, each with tunable boost parameters.

arxiv-2503-21436.title: Stochastic Engrams for Efficient Continual Learning
arxiv-2503-21436.creator: Isabelle Aguilar, Luis Fernando Herbozo Contreras, Omid Kavehei
arxiv-2503-21436.description: Abstract The ability to learn continuously in artificial neural networks (ANNs) is often limited by catastrophic forgetting, a phenomenon in which new knowledge becomes dominant. By taking mechanisms of memory encoding in neuroscience (i.e., engrams) as inspiration, we propose a novel approach that integrates stochastically-activated engrams as a gating mechanism for metaplastic binarized neural networks ( m BNNs).

arxiv-2504-20810.title: Effective Metric Description of Charged Black Holes
arxiv-2504-20810.creator: Mattia Damia Paciarini, Manuel Del Piano, Stefan Hohenegger, Francesco Sannino
arxiv-2504-20810.description: Abstract Charged black holes arise as solutions of General Relativity (GR) coupled to Maxwell theory. As functions of the mass and charge, they can exhibit extremal behavior, in which case they are stable against thermal decay. (Quantum) corrections to GR are expected to alter the classical features of these objects, especially near extremality.

arxiv-2505-06514.title: Direct space-time modeling of mechanically dressed dipole-dipole interactions with electromagnetically-coupled oscillating dipoles
arxiv-2505-06514.creator: Yi-Ming Chang, Kamran Akbari, Matthew Filipovich, Stephen Hughes
arxiv-2505-06514.description: Abstract We study the radiative dynamics of coupled electric dipoles, modelled as Lorentz oscillators (LOs), in the presence of real-time mechanical oscillations. The dipoles are treated in a self-consistent way through a direct electromagnetic simulation approach that fully includes the dynamical movement of the charges, accounting for radiation reaction, emission and absorption.

arxiv-2509-15640.title: Multilingual LLM Prompting Strategies for Medical English–Vietnamese Machine Translation
arxiv-2509-15640.creator: Nhu Vo 1,3 , Nu-Uyen-Phuong Le 2 , Dung D. Le 1 , Massimo Piccardi 3 , Wray Buntine 1 1 College of Engineering and Computer Science,VinUniversity,Vietnam 2 University of Queensland, Australia 3 University of Technology Sydney, Australia {nhu.vd,dung.ld,wray.b}@vinuni.edu.vn nuuyenphuong.le@student.u
arxiv-2509-15640.description: Abstract Medical English–Vietnamese machine translation (En–Vi MT) is essential for healthcare access and communication in Vietnam, yet Vietnamese remains a low-resource and under-studied language. We systematically evaluate prompting strategies for six multilingual LLMs (0.5B–9B parameters) on the MedEV dataset, comparing zero-shot, few-shot, and dictionary-augmented prompting with Meddict, an English–Vietnamese medical lexicon.

pmc-11418567.title: Hostel support workers’ experiences navigating healthcare alongside people experiencing homelessness: a qualitative study in the UK
pmc-11418567.creator: Iman Muzafar, Oliver Cunningham
pmc-11418567.description: ObjectivesThis study aimed to explore how hostel support workers (HSWs) experience navigating healthcare alongside people experiencing homelessness (PEH). PEH experience poor health outcomes, increased mortality and face many barriers when accessing healthcare. HSWs have a dynamic and holistic role, working with PEH to navigate access to health and social care, whilst facilitating independence.

pmc-11709564.title: Biological pathway‐based Alzheimer’s Disease polygenic risk score and proteinopathy
pmc-11709564.creator: Yuriko Katsumata, Xian Wu, Khine Zin Aung, Inori Tsuchiya, Lincoln MP Shade, Shama D Karanth, Kathryn Gauthreaux, Charles Mock, Walter A Kukull, Erin L Abner, Peter T Nelson, David W Fardo
pmc-11709564.description: BackgroundWe recently reported genetic associations with dementia‐related proteinopathies. Using multidimensional generalized partial credit modeling, we constructed three continuous latent variables, corresponding to TDP‐43, Aβ/Tau, and a‐synuclein related neuropathology endophenotype scores.MethodParticipant data were drawn from the National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center (NACC) neuropathology (NP) data (from the September 2023 data freeze) linked to Alzheimer’s Disease Genetics Consortium (ADGC) genotype data.

pmc-11713880.title: Daily care hours among older emergency department patients with dementia and undiagnosed cognitive impairment: a cross‐sectional study
pmc-11713880.creator: James Galske, Tonya Chera, Ula Hwang, Joan Monin, Arjun Venkatesh, Kenneth Lam, Amanda N Leggett, Cameron Gettel
pmc-11713880.description: BackgroundOver 15 million informal caregivers provide assistance to persons living with dementia. Despite increasing emergency department (ED) use within the population, little is known regarding the support required of older adults seeking acute care with varying degrees of cognitive impairment.

pmc-12732482.title: Deciphering the Role of DNA Polymerase Eta on the Incorporation and Bypass of Inosine and Cell Cycle Arrest
pmc-12732482.creator: Jackson C. Lin, Jameson R. Averill, Hunmin Jung
pmc-12732482.description: Inosine is a key intermediate in many cellular pathways, and our RT-qPCR data showed that DNA polymerase eta (polη) was upregulated upon the repeated treatment of inosine and inosine monophosphate (IMP) in HCT116 cells, which suggests that polη is actively involved in the incorporation and bypass of inosine in cells.

pmc-13299898.title: Impact of preprocedural imaging on outcomes of single-shot pulmonary vein isolation: a retrospective propensity score matched study
pmc-13299898.creator: N Soubh, B Hasan, E Rasenack, H Haarmann, F Wiedmann, M Zabel, C Schmidt, L Bergau
pmc-13299898.description: IntroductionSingle-shot pulmonary vein isolation (ssPVI) using cryoballoon ablation (CBA) or pulsed field ablation (PFA) is an established, effective, and safe therapy for patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). Preprocedural imaging (preIMG) with cardiac computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is commonly used to assess pulmonary vein (PV) anatomy.

pmc-13401295.title: Full genome sequencing, evolutionary dynamics, and pathogenicity evaluation of chicken infectious anemia virus with emphasis on Upper Egypt reveals genetic variability linked to vaccinal strains
pmc-13401295.creator: Eman Abd Elmenum Shosha, Ibrahim Eldaghayes, Ali Mahmoud Zanaty, Mohammed A. Gamaleldin, Mervat Masoud Mohamed, A. N. Gamal Maha, Doha Abd Alrahman Ahmed

pmc-13579893.title: Bioherbicidal activity and putative mode of action of Dittrichia graveolens against Amaranthus palmeri and A. retroflexus
pmc-13579893.creator: Mesut Sırrı, Ahlam Khalofah, Yunus Başar, Mustafa Abdullah Yılmaz, Shahid Farooq
pmc-13579893.description: BackgroundChallenges in controlling Amaranthus weeds and rising cases of herbicide resistance necessitate the development of alternative weed control strategies. Plant-derived extracts may serve as valuable sources of phytotoxic chemicals. Nevertheless, their species-specific effects on germination and early seedling development require investigation. This study evaluated the allelopathic activity of aqueous extracts of Dittrichia graveolens on Amaranthus palmeri and A. retroflexus.
